newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE to set Bosnia poll date for mid-September.
newsitem.headline: OSCE to set Bosnia poll date for mid-September.

text.p: Bosnia's municipal elections, originally planned for mid-July, are likely to be postponed to mid-September, a senior diplomat at the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said on Thursday.

"It is likely that today there will be a decision about a definitive date which would be the 13th and 14th of September," ambassador William Friis-Moller of Denmark, current chairman of the OSCE, told Reuters.
The 54-member OSCE, Europe's top security body, is in charge of organising the elections, viewed as Bosnia's last chance for reunification after a devastating 43-month war.
A meeting of the OSCE's permament council at the organisation's headquarters in Vienna would release an official statement on the election date later on Thursday, he said.

The local polls were originally to be held in September 1996, along with general elections, but were postponed because of widespread election fraud over refugee registration. They were moved to November last year and then to July this year.
Western countries funding the election had been pushing for a third postponement of the vote to allow more time to organise refugee registration and international monitoring.
Officials say the OSCE needs up to $55 million to organise the vote. The next round of nationwide elections are set for 1998, one year after the municipal vote in September.
